questions.q: What does it mean to be data-informed rather than data-driven?
a: Use data as input while you keep making the decisions
Let the numbers decide every choice for you
Collect data but never act on any of it
Ignore data until your company is profitable
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares data to a passenger, not the driver.

questions.q: What is data's main value to an entrepreneur, according to the summary?
a: It keeps you grounded and prevents self-delusion
It guarantees your product will sell
It replaces the need to talk to customers
It makes investors trust you more
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls data the antidote to delusion.

questions.q: What is the second stage in the summary's five-stage model?
a: Stickiness
Empathy
Virality
Revenue
questions.why: Lesson 2 orders the stages empathy, stickiness, virality, revenue and scale.

questions.q: What happens during the virality stage?
a: Features keep users returning and bring in their friends
The company enters new international markets
The team researches customer problems
The product starts charging customers money
questions.why: Lesson 2 says virality makes the product better through sharing.

questions.q: What is the One Metric That Matters?
a: The single key metric you track for your current stage
The metric your investors ask about most often
The first metric you ever measured for the business
A fixed number you never change over time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says shift the metric when you move to a new stage.
